title: Bound irreversible wrong-pair assembly using the actual access graph
statement: For n desired one-use handle pairs with intended rate k>0 and every ordered wrong partner rate beta>=0, an all-to-all constant-rate exponential race has Pcorrect=product_{j=0}^{n-1}(1+j*beta/k)^(-1). If instead every surviving state bounds each remaining site's aggregate wrong rate by D*beta while correct rate remains k, Pcorrect>=(1+D*beta/k)^(-n).

requires: Constant exponential hazards and one-use handles; any wrong bond is an absorbing product failure.
The bounded-access alternative requires the same D bound in EVERY surviving reaction state, not only initially.
provides: For n desired one-use handle pairs with intended rate k>0 and every ordered wrong partner rate beta>=0, an all-to-all constant-rate exponential race has Pcorrect=product_{j=0}^{n-1}(1+j*beta/k)^(-1). assumptions: All-to-all and bounded-access are distinct interfaces; the quadratic exponent is not a universal chemistry impossibility.
Packet product requires b dividing L, physical isolation and independently qualified connectors.
costs: All handle preparation, wrong products, isolation, connectors and finite-time completion remain charged; Pcorrect here concerns eventual competing-clock outcomes.
contract.units: k,beta are inverse time; beta/k and probabilities are dimensionless; n,L,b and D count pairs or bound access.
contract.obstruction: Acquire the actual spatial wrong-partner hazards and fusion interface before claiming long-program fidelity.

body: On an all-correct path with r pairs left, correct hazard is r*k and wrong hazard r*(r-1)*beta. Multiply the next-event correct probabilities as r decreases. For fixed n and small rho=beta/k, log Pcorrect=-rho*n*(n-1)/2+O(rho^2*n^3); this is not a uniform large-n asymptotic without controlling n*rho. With bounded access, next-event success is at least1/(1+D*rho); induction yields the alternative bound. For physically isolated b-edge packets and independent connector failure q, the separately assumed product law is Pcorrect(b)^(L/b)*(1-q)^(L/b-1). Neither the access bound nor independent fusion is supplied by a template label or small-packet success alone.
